tags.notes: Hirokawa Maru - 155m (508ft 6in) Japanese transport/freighter, beached 15 Nov 1942 during Guadalcanal campaign. Lies on port side. Bow at ~5m, stern at 55-60m. Shore entry from Bonegi Beach. Difficulty raised from Intermediate: stern at 55-60m is beyond standard recreational limits. RE-AUDIT 2026-09-18: Re-verified against McFadyen, DivePlanIt, Wannadive. Dimensions/depth confirmed (6872 tons, 508ft6in, stern 55-60m). Marine life in markdown trimmed to species confirmed by these sources (removed unconfirmed generic reef-fish padding).

Kinugawa Maru - 133m Japanese freighter, beached 15 Nov 1942. Lies upright. Bow in ~5-7m, stern at ~27m (sources: McFadyen, Wikipedia). Some sources give 23m. Easy circumnavigation, dense coral coverage. Shore entry Bonegi Beach. RE-AUDIT 2026-09-18: Re-verified against Wikipedia, McFadyen, DivePlanIt (6937 tons, 437ft/1931 build per DivePlanIt vs McFadyen 133m - both cited). Marine life trimmed to confirmed species (batfish, lionfish, multiple anemonefish/clownfish variants, hard/soft coral, gorgonians); removed unconfirmed anthias/chromis/scorpionfish/flatworms/octopus/whitetip shark claims.

140m Japanese transport ship, sunk by US submarine USS Searaven 25 Nov 1943. Lies on STARBOARD SIDE (not upright). Depth range 7-37m, stern at ~37m. Holds contain: Type 95 Ha-Go tanks, motorcycle sidecar combinations, sake bottles, ammunition, medical supplies. No gas masks documented. ~7km north of Gizo, ~20 min by boat. RE-AUDIT 2026-09-18: Cross-checked Wikipedia, DiveGizo, DivePlanIt. LENGTH CONFLICT: Wikipedia gives 153.1m (502.3ft)/10,052 tons; prior note used 140m - both figures now presented as a range in markdown. DEPTH CONFLICT: Wikipedia states stern at 40m/top at 12m; DiveGizo states 7-37m - both ranges now noted in markdown. Marine life trimmed to confirmed species only (turtles, rays, regal angelfish, spinecheek anemonefish, nudibranchs, anemones); removed unconfirmed glassy sweepers/grouper/Napoleon wrasse/lionfish/scorpionfish/whitetip shark/barracuda claims. Additionally, DiveGizo identifies the tank as a Type 21 vs. the original note's Type 95 Ha-Go, and describes a single motorbike rather than multiple motorcycle sidecar combinations - conflict now reflected in markdown rather than picking one.

Channel drift dive, Florida Islands area NE of Honiara, near Maravagi Bay. RE-AUDIT 2026-09-18: Independent cross-check (Master Liveaboards, PADI Travel blog) confirms this is widely described as the premier MANTA RAY dive in the Solomon Islands - up to a dozen mantas in formation, current 8-10 knots. Prior markdown omitted mantas entirely and led with grey reef sharks/eagle rays/barracuda (retained as secondary/plausible per bilikiki.com/dive-the-world.com, but manta rays are now the headline species per multiple independent sources). Markdown rewritten accordingly.

Marovo Lagoon wall dive, steep walls with sea fans, barracuda, jacks schools. Exceptional water clarity. RE-AUDIT 2026-09-18: Bilikiki Cruises (primary operator source) confirms this uninhabited island site for hard corals, large schools of fish, sharks, turtles, and bumphead parrotfish. Markdown marine life list trimmed to these confirmed categories; removed unconfirmed specifics (staghorn/Porites corals, surgeonfish, grouper, wire corals, crinoids, hawkfish, whitetip/grey reef shark species-level claims, eagle rays, trevally, Napoleon wrasse, moray eels, nudibranchs). RE-AUDIT 2026-09-18 - COORDINATE CORRECTION: prior coordinates (-9.3833, 160.1833) placed this site in the Florida Islands/Guadalcanal longitude range (~160.2E), roughly 150km from its actual location. Wikipedia confirms Mborokua (aka Mary Island) sits at 9 01S 158 44E - an uninhabited volcanic island in Western Province, roughly halfway between the Russell Islands and Marovo Lagoon (not literally inside the lagoon). Corrected coordinates and description accordingly.

CORRECTED LOCATION: Eastern Russell Islands (NOT Florida Islands as previously stated - coordinates are approximate for Russell Islands). Narrow volcanic chasm on Leru Island. ~100m passage at 12-23m depth, open sky above, sunlight shafts. Lobsters/crayfish at end of cut, pygmy seahorses on sea fans at entrance. Liveaboard access only. One of the most-photographed sites in the Solomon Islands. RE-AUDIT 2026-09-18 - COORDINATE CORRECTION: prior coordinates (-9.0833, 160.25) placed this site in Florida Islands longitude range (~160E), but Leru Island is documented (DivePlanIt, Tripadvisor, DAN) as being in the Russell Islands, north of Pavuvu Island (Pavuvu is at approx -9.067, 159.118). Corrected to an approximate position within the Russell Islands (~159.15E). Precise GPS for Leru Island was not found in any source consulted; local operator confirmation recommended.

RE-AUDIT 2026-09-18: Deep re-audit could not independently confirm 'Maravagi Passage' as a named current-drift site. Bilikiki Cruises' actual site listing documents a DIFFERENT, nearby site called 'Maravagi Bay' described as a calm macro-diving location (nudibranchs, scorpionfish, pipefish, cuttlefish, anemone fish, seagrass/sand channels) - the opposite profile from the strong-current drift dive with sharks/barracuda/trevally previously described here. dive-the-world.com's site list does not include this name either. It is unclear whether 'Maravagi Passage' is an informal/alternate name for a current channel near Maravagi Bay, a conflation with 'Maravagi Bay' itself, or a distinct site entirely. Per deep-QA policy (3+ independent sources required to keep validated=true), downgrading to validated=false pending a source that specifically documents a channel/passage by this name.

COORDINATES CORRECTED by ~250km: Sandfly Passage is between Nggela Sule and Mbokonimbeti/Olevugha Islands (Florida Islands / Guadalcanal Province) at approx -9.03, 160.08. Previous coordinates (-8.08, 156.85) incorrectly placed it near Gizo/Western Province. Wall/drift dive 3-40m with large sea fans, strong tidal currents, manta rays, nudibranchs, fusilier schools. Simon's Nature Reserve (80+ coral genera) is within the passage. MS World Discoverer ran aground here in 2000. RE-AUDIT 2026-09-18: Independent source (UW Photography Guide destination roundup, corroborating aggregated travel-press coverage) attributes manta ray sightings (up to a dozen, feeding in formation) to the Mbike & Sandfly Passage channel system - consistent with the original validation note's mention of manta rays, which the markdown had omitted. Markdown updated to restore manta rays alongside grey reef sharks. Note: manta megadive descriptions in travel press are sometimes attributed to 'Devil's Highway' and sometimes to 'Sandfly Passage'/'Mbike Passage' for this same general Nggela current system - flagged as a naming ambiguity rather than resolved fact.

RE-AUDIT 2026-09-18: Deep re-audit could not independently confirm this named site in any source. Direct checks of bilikiki.com/about/dive-sites and dive-the-world.com/diving-sites-solomon-islands.php (both previously cited) do NOT list a 'Custom's House Wreck'; visitsolomons.com.sb PDF is image-based and could not be text-verified; targeted web searches for 'Custom's House wreck Honiara' and similar returned no matches. Per deep-QA policy (3+ independent sources required to keep validated=true, no padding with unverifiable sources), downgrading to validated=false. Site kept in the dataset (plausible small local harbour wreck) but flagged unresolved pending a source that specifically documents it.

RE-AUDIT 2026-09-18 - MAJOR CORRECTION: Original entry described a halocline/freshwater-over-saltwater 'mirror reflection' feature at Uepi Island Resort, Marovo Lagoon. This could not be corroborated and is contradicted by three independent sources (DivePlanIt, Bilikiki Cruises, LiveAboard.com aggregator), which all identify 'Mirror Pond' as a swim-through/cave-and-wall dive site on MANE ISLAND, RUSSELL ISLANDS (~50km NW of Honiara) - an entirely different location and site type, with no halocline/mirror-reflection optical effect described anywhere. Corrected: location to Mane Island, Russell Islands (precise GPS not published in any source consulted - coordinates are an approximate placement within the Russell Islands group and should be refined by a local operator); depth to median 9m/max 25m (DivePlanIt); site description to swim-through with shafts of light leading to a surface pond, adjacent wall. Marine life corrected to confirmed species only (barracuda, flame angelfish, anemonefish, crocodilefish per DivePlanIt/Bilikiki) - removed the fabricated halocline/freshwater-lens content entirely.

tags.name: Kyusyu Maru
tags.notes: Japanese passenger-cargo ship 142m long, 8666 tons. Beached after bombing attack circa 14-15 Oct 1942 (date conflict: dive sources say Oct 15; IJN records CombinedFleet.com say Oct 14). Also known as 'Ruinin Wreck' or 'Bonegi 3'. Lies on PORT SIDE at 45 degrees, 3m to 46m. Hold contains: rifle rounds, cattle bones, china. NOT same as Toa Maru. RE-AUDIT 2026-09-18: Re-verified against McFadyen (primary), Pacific Wrecks, CombinedFleet.com. Cargo contents (rifle rounds, biscuits, china, cattle bones), dimensions (8666 tons/467ft), and depth range (3-45/46m) all reconfirmed.

tags.name: Japanese Submarine I-1
tags.notes: Junsen Type 1 (J1 class) cruiser submarine, ~319-320ft, 2135 tons. Rammed three times by HMNZS Kiwi on night of 29-30 Jan 1943 in Kamimbo Bay area (ran aground at Fish Reef, ~330 yards north of Kamimbo Bay). Salvage (late 1960s) destroyed forward third. Remaining aft section: 5-30m (McFadyen); Wikipedia gives bow at ~14m. War grave. RE-AUDIT 2026-09-18: A third independent source (UW Photography Guide) gives stern ~25m/top ~10m, slightly different from McFadyen's bow 5m/stern 30m and Wikipedia's bow ~14m. Depth figures vary by source (roughly 5-14m shallow point, 25-30m stern) - noted as a range rather than picking one figure.

tags.name: B-17 Flying Fortress
tags.notes: B-17E serial 41-2420 'Bessie the Jap Basher', 42nd Bombardment Squadron/11th Bombardment Group. Ditched 24 Sep 1942 returning from mission over Shortland/Bougainville area, hit by Japanese Zero fighters. Location: Doma Cove (Ndomo), ~12 miles east of Henderson Field. Crew of 9, entire crew initially listed MIA. RE-AUDIT 2026-09-18 (HIGH-RISK WWII AIRCRAFT ITEM, cross-checked McFadyen + Pacific Wrecks crew-record page + Emperor Divers): CORRECTED RANK - pilot was 1st Lt. Charles E. Norton, NOT 'Captain' as prior markdown stated. Fate of Norton and gunner Sgt. Bruce W. Osborne is not fully documented; Pacific Wrecks states they were 'possibly' executed after capture, Osborne's remains recovered by Seabees Jan 1944 - written as a hedge, not a stated fact. Tail section salvage by Seabees in 1944 remains a single-source (JSON-only) claim not independently re-confirmed this pass; retained with appropriate caution. Port wing 17m/starboard wing 9m depths reconfirmed by McFadyen.

tags.name: USS John Penn
tags.notes: US Naval Transport AP-51 (later APA-23), formerly SS Excambion (1931, American Export Lines). Torpedoed by Japanese Kate bombers 13 Aug 1943 off Lunga Point. Lies on starboard side; shallowest point ~36m, sand bottom ~56-58m. Japanese aircraft wreck near bridge/deck junction at ~60m (believed to be a Kate - single source, McFadyen describes it as 'I believe'). Jeep found ~20m from main hull. War grave. RE-AUDIT 2026-09-18: McFadyen re-confirms Kate aircraft find was made by diver Jason McHattan at the deck/bridge junction, ~60m - still a single-diver identification, hedge retained. Jeep provenance (originally an Army base vehicle from New Caledonia) is an additional McFadyen detail, not independently cross-referenced elsewhere - not added to markdown as a confirmed fact for that reason. Main wreck depths (shallow ~36m, main hull ~56-58m, stern section ~400m away) reconfirmed.

tags.name: Tambea Caves
tags.notes: Cave system near Tambea village, ~40km west of Honiara, Guadalcanal coast. ~6 interconnected caves, passages 1-2m wide, at least one tight squeeze. Guide-led dive. Max 15m, ~24m visibility outside. Overhead environment. RE-AUDIT 2026-09-18: McFadyen reconfirms ~6 interconnected caves/tunnels, 1-2m passage width with a tight squeeze, 24m outside visibility. Depth (15m) not explicitly stated in McFadyen text; retained per bilikiki.com/visitsolomons.com.sb general guides. No marine life details found beyond a single gorgonia in a photo caption - markdown correctly has no fabricated species list.

tags.name: Sea Lark Channel
tags.notes: Drift dive along Sealark Reef east of Honiara on incoming tide. Reef drops surface to 30m+. Large gorgonian sea fans bent by persistent current. Napoleon (humphead) wrasse along reef edge. 50-60 min drift, 2+ knots at bends. ~25m visibility. RE-AUDIT 2026-09-18: McFadyen source explicitly states 'fishlife is not overly prolific' at this site despite the coral/current features - markdown's claim that current attracts schooling fish and reef predators was overstated and has been removed. Confirmed features retained: gorgonian sea fans, feather-stars, hump-headed (Napoleon) wrasse, current 2+ knots at bends.

tags.name: HMNZS Moa
tags.notes: New Zealand Bird-class minesweeper, 51.2m (168ft) long, 607 tons standard displacement (NOT 825 tons - unsupported figure). Sunk 7 April 1943 by Japanese Aichi D3A Val dive bombers during Operation I-Go at Tulagi. Direct bomb hit through captain's cabin, sank within ~4 minutes. 5 crew killed. Wreck upright at ~40m with slight port list. 4-inch bow gun, anti-aircraft gun, twin depth charge racks, bomb hole in starboard hull all visible. War grave. RE-AUDIT 2026-09-18: Re-confirmed via Wikipedia/NZ History/McFadyen. GPS position from McFadyen (S9 05 42.1, E160 08 57.2) matches our recorded coordinates exactly. Firefish sighting is specifically reported in the engine room area (McFadyen), not "throughout the wreck" as prior markdown stated - narrowed accordingly.

tags.name: Kawanishi Mavis Flying Boat
tags.notes: Kawanishi H6K 'Mavis' four-engine flying boats attacked at Ghavutu-Tanambogo 7 Aug 1942 (opening day of Guadalcanal invasion). 7 H6K aircraft plus 8 Rufe floatplanes were present (total 15 aircraft, not '10-13' as previously stated); destroyed by F4F Wildcats in surprise dawn raid. Best two Mavis wrecks at 30-34m off Tanambogo Island. Wingspan ~40m confirmed for H6K. Cockpit instruments, reconnaissance camera may still be visible. War grave. RE-AUDIT 2026-09-18: McFadyen states 10-13 diveable Mavis WRECKS exist at the site today (a count of wrecks, distinct from the 7 Mavis + reported Rufe floatplanes present during the 7 Aug 1942 attack). Markdown already kept these separate; no factual change needed. Mavis No. 2 depth (~30m, "just over 30m") and near-intact condition reconfirmed.

tags.name: Twin Tunnels
tags.notes: Near Tulagi (~1km SE of Tulagi Island), Florida Islands. Two vertical lava tubes dropping from seamount plateau (12-16m) to junction cave/chamber at ~34-36m with crayfish. Reef rises from 70m+ depth. NOTE: 'Bayldon Shoals' is a SEPARATE nearby site (long shallow reef 18m top, SW wall); 'Soghonangola Island' is unverifiable in geographic sources. Grey reef sharks, whitetip sharks, fusiliers, trevally, snappers, multiple anemonefish species. RE-AUDIT 2026-09-18: McFadyen reconfirms location (GPS S9 08 49.5, E160 08 31.3 matches our coordinates exactly), depth profile (12m top / 35m junction / 45m+ edge), and marine life (whitetip/grey reef sharks, fusiliers, rainbow runners, crayfish in mid-tunnel cave). Additional confirmed but not previously listed: barrel sponges, clown triggerfish.

tags.name: USS Aaron Ward
tags.notes: Gleaves-class destroyer (Bristol sub-group) DD-483, 348 feet long. CORRECTED SINKING DATE: Sunk 7 April 1943 by Japanese dive bombers during Operation I-Go near Tinete Point, Nggela Sule (NOT sunk 13 Nov 1942 during First Naval Battle of Guadalcanal - she survived that battle damaged). Wreck upright, deck at ~63m, deepest ~70m. Technical dive only. Guns, torpedo tubes, depth charge racks visible. War grave. RE-AUDIT 2026-09-18: Re-confirmed via McFadyen, Wikipedia, DestroyerHistory.org - sinking date/cause (Operation I-Go, 7 April 1943, dive bombers), depth (~70m, sandy bottom), and the distinction from her survival of the Nov 1942 surface battle. Wreck discovered 1991 by Robert Ballard, first dived 1994 (Gardner/Bailey) - new corroborating detail, not previously in notes.

tags.name: Hundred Thousand Dollar Point
tags.notes: Northern end of Tulagi Island. Post-WWII Allied equipment dump documented by McFadyen (page_id=388): trucks incl. 6-wheel drive, jeeps, engines, wheels, pontoons, Coca-Cola bottles, girders, trailers. NOTE: name not found in any other published dive guide - locally also called 'Base 1' or 'Ship Dump'. Different from Vanuatu's 'Million Dollar Point'. RE-AUDIT 2026-09-18 - DEPTH CORRECTED: re-fetched the actual McFadyen source page (the same page previously cited as primary source) and it explicitly states the debris field extends 'to a depth of about 30 to 35 metres' - this contradicts the prior QA pass's un-sourced reduction to 26m. Restored depth to 35m (upper end of McFadyen's own stated range) since that is the only site-specific depth figure with a named, checkable source; markdown notes the 30-35m range explicitly.
tags.depth_range_note: 30-35m per McFadyen (primary, dedicated page); some general destination guides implied shallower ~20-26m without specific sourcing

tags.name: Grumman Hellcat
tags.notes: F6F-3 Hellcat serial 25389. Shot down 16 Sep 1943 by friendly fire from Major Gregory 'Pappy' Boyington (flying F4U Corsair). Location: 3km south of Kolombangara in Blackett Strait, near Queue (Quomu) Island. Fully intact at 11m, flaps down, cockpit open with instruments. Starboard wing buried in coral. Discovered 1985. Confirmed by McFadyen and pacificwrecks.com. RE-AUDIT 2026-09-18: McFadyen names the pilot as Lieutenant Dick Moore, who ditched successfully after Boyington's friendly-fire hit caused an oil leak, and was rescued by local islanders and an Australian coastwatcher - confirmed detail added to markdown (pilot survived; this is not a war grave in the sense of a fatal loss).

tags.name: Grand Central Station
tags.notes: Signature reef dive of Gizo area, WNW of Toa Maru wreck. Best in strong current: whitetip and grey reef sharks, barracuda schools, giant sweetlips, clown and titan triggerfish. 30-35m. RE-AUDIT 2026-09-18: McFadyen reconfirms depth ("over 35m but 30m is deep enough") and marine life (whitetip/grey reef sharks, barracuda, clown/titan triggerfish, giant sweetlips) and the "needs strong current" character. No changes required.

tags.name: The Gap
tags.notes: SE corner of Ghizo Island, main entrance to Gizo Harbour. Wall dive with huge gorgonian sea fans, basket sponges, thousands of garden eels on sandy bottom. Eagle rays, grey reef sharks, barracuda, tuna, trevally. 30m+ visibility. CORRECTED site_type from reef to wall. RE-AUDIT 2026-09-18: McFadyen reconfirms depth (reef top ~9m, wall 30-35m+), marine life (garden eels, eagle rays, grey reef shark, barracuda, tuna, trevally), and strong tidal current at the harbour entrance. No changes required.

tags.name: Top Secret Place
tags.notes: South of Nusa Aghana Island, SE Ferguson Passage, ~20 min from Gizo. Wall drops 60m+. Known for manta rays, large rays, grey reef sharks, sea snakes. 40m+ visibility at depth. CORRECTED site_type from reef to wall. RE-AUDIT 2026-09-18: McFadyen reconfirms wall depth (60m+), visibility (30-40m+), and marine life (manta ray sighted at distance, large rays, grey reef shark, yellow-and-black sea snake). No changes required.

tags.name: MV Roylen Petaj
tags.notes: Former RAN Fairmile motor launch ML 805, 112 feet (34m), 75 tons. Scuttled in Gizo Harbour. Lists to starboard at 14m. Batfish, lionfish, trevally. 2008 tsunami may have altered condition. RE-AUDIT 2026-09-18: McFadyen reconfirms dimensions (112ft Fairmile launch, 75 tons), depth (stern 12m/bow 14m), marine life (trevally, batfish under port side, firefish in engine room - all reconfirmed) and history (hosted Japanese surrender ceremonies 1945 - new corroborating detail, not added to markdown as it needs a second source).

tags.name: Tokuyo Maru
tags.notes: Japanese fishing trawler ~40m long, sunk 24 Dec 1987 near Ferguson Passage after locals moved a channel marker. Lies on port side at 38m. Name still visible on stern. Modern vessel, not a war wreck. Primarily documented by McFadyen (page_id=394). RE-AUDIT 2026-09-18: McFadyen (full name "Tokuyo Maru No 11") reconfirms 40m length, 24 Dec 1987 sinking after reef strike (a dislodged depth-sounder transponder created the hull breach), depth ~38m. No marine life documented in source; markdown correctly has none.

tags.name: USS Kanawha
tags.notes: Fleet oiler AO-1, 145m long (475ft 7in - NOT 137m as previously stated). Attacked by Japanese Val dive bombers 7 April 1943 during Operation I-Go, same raid as HMNZS Moa and USS Aaron Ward. Slid off beached position and sank early 8 April 1943. Upright facing south near Tulagi. Multiple gun positions at 43-48m, propellers buried at 57-58m. 19 crew lost. War grave. RE-AUDIT 2026-09-18: Wikipedia independently confirms length 475ft7in/144.96m (matches our 145m figure) and 19 crew lost - the McFadyen page itself has an apparent typo ("457 feet 7 inches") which is superseded by the Wikipedia/NavSource figure already in use. No marine life documented in either source; markdown correctly has none.

tags.name: USS Minneapolis Bow
tags.notes: Severed bow of New Orleans-class heavy cruiser USS Minneapolis CA-36. Bow cut off after two torpedo hits at Battle of Tassafaronga 30 Nov 1942. Ship reached Tulagi; Navy divers and Seabees cut the bow free where it sank. Lies inverted (upside-down) at 15-20m facing out from shore. China plates, portlights, landing craft and WWII debris on surrounding seabed. War grave. RE-AUDIT 2026-09-18: McFadyen reconfirms severed-bow account, inverted orientation, and debris (china plates, portlights, landing craft). NEW SAFETY-RELEVANT DETAIL from source: 50-100 live/unexploded 8-inch naval shells lie nearby (20-22m depth, NE of the bow) - added to Safety Considerations in markdown as this is a genuine hazard (unexploded ordnance), not merely decorative debris.

tags.name: Mitsubishi Zero Gizo
tags.notes: A6M Zero fighter off Gizo market near Catholic Cathedral, 8-10m. Guns and instruments removed; landing gear down (inconsistent with water landing, suggests placed here). Fuselage broken behind cockpit, tail inverted nearby, port wing buried. Canopy and basic airframe identifiable. RE-AUDIT 2026-09-18: McFadyen reconfirms depth (8-10m), condition (fuselage broken behind cockpit, tail inverted, port wing buried in sand, no guns/instruments, landing gear down), and location (off Gizo market, near Catholic Cathedral). No marine life documented in source; markdown correctly has none.
